My `write_file` calls didn't show content, and your pytest run was the only evidence that anything changed. I'll re-check the date parser first.

TOOL: read_file utils/dates.py
TOOL: read_file tests/test_dates.py
TOOL: bash git -C . status --short && git -C . diff --stat

Next I'll locate the signup form in the other repo so I can see its structure before editing it.

TOOL: bash ls ../web-landing && git -C ../web-landing status --short
TOOL: bash grep -ril "signup\|sign-up\|sign_up" ../web-landing --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=.git | head -50

Once I have the results, I'll confirm the date fix against the actual files, then look at the form's markup and its submit handler before adding the consent checkbox. I'll also ask you what the consent wording should be and whether it needs to be legally reviewed, since the checkbox text is a compliance decision and I shouldn't invent it.
